t001: Fade the blemish. Keep the skin.
t002: Free, open-source portrait retouching that runs entirely on your own device. Your photos are never uploaded.
t003: Real LRCDF output, one click, no hand edits
t005: Retouching works by frequency separation. Colour and light are evened in one layer, while the fine texture sits in another and is only reduced on the blemishes themselves. Skin still looks like skin.
t006: Zoomed in on the same cheek. Large raised spots may not disappear completely, so some marks stay faintly visible. For those, finish by hand.
t008: Retouching doesn’t make anyone lighter. If you can barely tell the two sides apart here, that’s the point. Colour looks are also held back on faces that read as dark, so they keep their own depth.
t009: Toning still corrects exposure. An under-exposed or backlit face can get brighter along with the rest of the photo, and you can pull that back with the brightness control.
t010: Everyone in the photo gets their own setting.
t011: LRCDF recognises the people across a shoot. Choose a level for each of them, including no retouching at all. Here the woman on the left was left alone.
t012: Tonewell does this too on Mac and iPad, not yet on Windows.
t014: A look’s orange and yellow skin corrections are applied to skin alone, so warm clothes, props and backgrounds aren’t thinned out with it.
t015: Paint or make-up on skin counts as skin and can soften a little.
t017: If your photos already live in Lightroom Classic, use LRCDF. If they don’t, Tonewell does the job on its own.
t025: A new TIFF stacked above the original in your catalogue
t026: New files saved separately; originals untouched
t041: Learns a look from your edits
t044: Flags closed eyes and soft focus
t049: iPad only: USB (Sony A7R V) or the camera’s FTP transfer over Wi-Fi. Tested with a Sony A7R V.
t054: Downloads are on the project’s GitHub releases page, where each release lists its files and install steps.
t057: There is no paid tier and no account. The source code is Apache-2.0. Model weights come with the apps and have their own terms, listed in the repository.
t059: All toning and retouching happens on your device, and no photo is ever uploaded. The apps check for updates, which sends nothing about you and can be switched off. One exception: a Google library inside LRCDF sends usage statistics, without photos, to Google while it looks for faces. Tonewell sends nothing of the kind. The privacy policy has the details.
t061: This is independent software, not a company’s product, so expect rough edges. If a photo comes out wrong or an install gets stuck, please open an issue.
t063: The apps aren’t signed by Apple, so macOS blocks them the first time. Go to System Settings, then Privacy & Security, and choose Open Anyway. You only do this once.
t065: The direct downloads aren’t signed for Windows, so Windows may show a warning the first time. LRCDF installs by running the included script in PowerShell. Tonewell needs no installer: extract both downloads into the same folder and run it. No administrator rights are needed. Tonewell from the Microsoft Store shows no warning; LRCDF is not in the Store.
t067: Tonewell isn’t on the App Store, so you sideload it. With a free Apple Account it has to be reinstalled every 7 days. The install guide can be handed to an AI assistant to walk you through it.

title: LRCDF and Tonewell: free portrait retouching on your own computer
description: Free, open-source portrait retouching that fades blemishes, keeps real skin texture and runs entirely on your own device. For Lightroom Classic, or as a standalone app for Mac, iPad and Windows.
t141: Windows 11, 64-bit. The same Tonewell, installed and kept up to date by the Store.
t142: About 3.5 GB. No warning on first launch and nothing to extract.
